::: {.callout-important}
## Not everything on the website is assigned

The site contains a complete teaching and practice bank. In a normal week,
students are expected to follow the two class meetings, complete the parts of
the main lab selected in class, and attempt the **core exercises** listed
below. Guided and extension material is available for support and further
practice; it is not automatically due.
:::

## The Three Workload Labels

| Label | What it means for students |
|---|---|
| **Core** | Essential work. Participate in the in-class workflow and attempt these exercises independently. Core does not mean that every item must be submitted. |
| **Guided** | Work used selectively in class, office hours, tutorials, or a Blackboard announcement. Complete it when the instructor assigns it or when you need more practice. |
| **Extension** | Optional breadth or challenge. It is not assumed knowledge for the next week unless the instructor announces otherwise. |

Slides, examples, checklists, and complete lab instructions remain available as
reference material. Their presence on the website does not make every line a
separate task.

## The Default Week

Unless a Blackboard announcement says otherwise, the normal rhythm is:

1. take part in the two scheduled class meetings;
2. work through the instructor-selected checkpoints of the week's main lab;
3. attempt the 4-6 core exercises listed below;
4. complete the short in-class exit check;
5. use guided exercises for recovery or consolidation;
6. complete an AI-review lab only when it is embedded in class or explicitly
   assigned.

The target for routine website-based practice outside class is approximately
**90-120 minutes in an ordinary week**. This target does not include separately
announced project work or preparation for a quiz, midterm, or final
examination.

Assessment weeks use a reduced teaching and practice selection when an
assessment displaces normal class time. The [Quiz 1 guide](../assessments/quiz-01.qmd)
is available now; later assessment formats will be announced before they are
needed. Students will not be expected to complete a full ordinary week on top
of displaced class time.

## How Labs Fit

- The numbered main lab for each week is the **guided core workflow**. The
  instructor selects its checkpoints; the whole file is not automatically
  additional homework.
- Labs ending in **B** are **guided AI audits**. They are embedded in a meeting
  or assigned selectively rather than added as a second full weekly lab.
- [Lab 4A: ODE solver checks](../labs/lab-04-ode-mini.qmd) is an **extension or
  alternate** activity.
- Project work has its own [instructions and milestones](../projects/project-milestones.qmd).
  It is not hidden inside the weekly lab expectation.

## If You Are Behind

Do the work in this order:

1. read the week's computational question and survival checklist;
2. rerun the main example or starter script;
3. complete the main-lab checkpoints identified by the instructor;
4. attempt the core exercises;
5. use guided work only where it addresses a specific difficulty;
6. leave extension work until the core is secure.

Ask for help when a core task remains blocked after one serious attempt. The
goal is a checked workflow that you understand, not completion of every page on
the site.
